summary.text: A discrete uniform distribution has a known, finite number of outcomes that are all equally likely to happen.
With n outcomes, each one has probability 1/n, so a fair six-sided die gives every face a chance of 1/6.
Not everything built from dice is uniform: adding the values of two thrown dice gives sums that are not equally likely.

facts.label: Not just numbers
facts.value: Works over any finite set, even symbols on die faces

facts.label: Two-dice sums
facts.value: Not uniform, since sums differ in probability

items.prompt: A raffle has 20 tickets and each is equally likely to be drawn. What is the chance that one particular ticket wins?
items.explain: With n equally likely outcomes, each has probability 1/n, so one of 20 tickets has 1/20.

items.prompt: You roll two fair dice and add the spots. Is each possible total equally likely?

options.label: Yes, because each die is fair, every total shares the same chance
Yes, because there are only a few totals to land on
No, the totals do not all have the same probability
No, because one die always affects the total more

items.explain: Each die alone is uniform, but the sums of two dice would not have equal probability, so the distribution of totals is not uniform.

items.prompt: A game uses a fair die with six different animal pictures instead of numbers. How likely is each picture on a throw?

options.label: It depends on how common the animal is
Pictures cannot be uniform since they are not numbers
Each has chance 1 out of 2
Each has chance 1/6, just like numbered faces

items.explain: A uniform distribution can be defined over any finite set, and six equally likely faces each have probability 1/6.

items.prompt: A friend says a setup is a discrete uniform distribution. What must be true of its outcomes?

options.label: There is a known, finite number of them, all equally likely
There are infinitely many, all equally likely
There are a few, with the first one most likely
There are a finite number, and they pair up symmetrically

items.explain: The idea is a known, finite number of outcomes that are all equally likely.

items.prompt: A fair 6-sided die is swapped for a fair 12-sided die. What happens to the chance of landing on any one particular face?

options.label: It doubles
It stays the same
It halves, from 1/6 to 1/12
It drops to zero

items.explain: Each face has probability 1/n for n equally likely faces, so going from 6 faces to 12 halves the chance.

items.prompt: A teacher says a uniform draw must use consecutive whole numbers like 1 through 6. Is she right?

options.label: No, any finite set of outcomes can be used
Yes, only whole numbers in a row can be equally likely
Yes, but only if there are exactly six
No, but it must at least use numbers

items.explain: Consecutive integers are common, but discrete uniform distributions can be defined over any finite set, even abstract symbols.
